title: Config Sensitivity Prober & Auto-Revert for Canary/A-B Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight probabilistic configuration sensitivity prober that fuzzes small, controlled changes to model and runtime configs (temperature, max_tokens, quantization profile, batch-size limits) during canary and A/B rollouts. The prober will measure regression likelihoods using existing eval suites and a small production cohort, compute confidence intervals for key quality metrics, and feed signals to an Auto-Revert policy that can automatically pause or roll back the rollout when regressions exceed calibrated thresholds. This reduces silent regressions caused by subtle config/model interactions and gives SREs/PMs a deterministic, auditable decision path for automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prober runs as part of canary and A/B traffic splits and performs controlled perturbations without exceeding latency SLOs.
- Computes 95% confidence intervals for each tracked metric and reports probability of regression > baseline.
- Auto-Revert policy triggers a safe rollback or pause when probability of degradation > configured threshold for two consecutive windows.
- All triggers are logged with root-cause candidates and a replayable event for investigation.
- Unit/integration tests + end-to-end smoke test against staging that demonstrates rollback on synthetic regression.
- Console dashboard shows prober trends, CI bands, and recent automatic actions.
design_decisions:
- Use existing eval harness and small production sampler; prefer statistical tests (bootstrap CI) over single-threshold heuristics so small cohorts don't create false positives.
- Perturbations limited to one parameter at a time and bounded by safe ranges to avoid customer-facing regression spikes.
- Rollback policy requires two consecutive windows (e.g., 2 x 5m) with prob(regression) > 0.9 to reduce flapping.
- Provide human-in-the-loop override and a review queue to approve/undo automatic reverts.
- Store prober runs and decisions in the rollout audit log for compliance and postmortem analyses.
implementation_plan:
1) Add "config prober" module in runtime control plane to schedule and execute perturbations on canary cohorts.
2) Integrate prober outputs into Eval Service; extend existing eval APIs to return bootstrap CIs and regression probabilities.
3) Implement Auto-Revert controller that subscribes to eval signals and enforces rollback windows and cooldowns.
4) Add observability: dashboard panels, alert rules, and audit entries.
5) End-to-end tests, chaos testing in staging, and runbook updates.
6) Gradual rollout behind feature flag with metrics collected for 2 weeks before enabling auto-revert for all teams.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for prober perturbation generator and safe-range enforcement.
- Integration tests: prober+eval service returns expected CIs on synthetic datasets.
- Staging e2e: deploy a synthetic bad model and verify Auto-Revert triggers and rollback timeline.
- Canary burn-in: Enable prober in 10% of canaries and monitor false positive rate < 2%.
- Post-deploy A/B run with supervised human checks for first 48h when auto-revert is enabled.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Feature flag off (internal QA).
Phase 2: Flag on for internal teams and non-critical customers (10% of canaries).
Phase 3: Expand to 50% after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
Phase 4: Enable Auto-Revert for high-risk releases only; eventually default on for runtime-1.22+.
Include gradual increases in perturbation coverage and shorten evaluation windows only after FP rate and latency impact are validated.
monitoring_queries:
- prober.run_count: count by rollout_id over 5m windows
- eval.metric.delta: distribution of metric deltas vs baseline
- eval.metric.bootstrap_ci: lower/upper bound series
- auto_revert.actions: count and reason labels
- rollback.latency: time from trigger to full revert
- false_positive.rate: fraction of auto_revert actions deemed unnecessary after human review

notes: This ticket focuses on config sensitivity (small param changes) rather than full-model A/B synthetic testing. For large-model swaps we keep the existing cohort eval checkpoints but will reuse prober's CI infrastructure to standardize signals. Ensure auditability for compliance teams; store raw prober inputs and eval outputs for 90 days.
